candidate.educational_objective: Apply current authoritative guidance to identify the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response for the clinical construct tested by V2-Q0162.

options.A: Delay vasopressor therapy until a central venous catheter is placed because peripheral administration is not recommended in septic shock.
options.B: Start norepinephrine promptly through an appropriate peripheral IV under a safety-monitoring protocol rather than delaying vasopressor initiation solely to obtain central access.
options.C: Use dopamine as the routine first-line vasopressor because it is preferred over norepinephrine when central access is unavailable.
options.D: Continue giving repeated fixed-volume crystalloid boluses until central access is secured because vasopressors should begin only after hypotension resolves.

candidate.rationale: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign suggests starting vasopressors peripherally in septic shock rather than delaying treatment until central venous access is secured, and recommends norepinephrine as the first-line vasopressor. Peripheral use should occur with appropriate monitoring and a safety protocol because extravasation remains a recognized risk.

candidate.stem: An adult with septic shock remains hypotensive after initial crystalloid resuscitation. Vasopressor therapy is indicated, but central venous access has not yet been obtained. Which action best reflects the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign?
